infra.list.toolbar.newManualHint: Needs an access key ID + secret
infra.list.empty: No AWS profiles yet. If you only have an account + password, use Console sign-in; if you already have ~/.aws, use Import.
infra.list.detail.choose: Choose a profile to see its details.
infra.list.action.editDisabledProcess: Read-only — this profile runs a credential_process command, which AWOG cannot edit in v1.
infra.list.value.regionUnset: Not set (AWS CLI will report a missing Region)
infra.list.process.note: This profile runs an external credential_process command. AWOG only reads AWS profiles that carry one (v1) — the command text itself lives in the file below, not in this app.
infra.list.unknown.note: AWOG could not tell this profile's kind from the keys it read — nothing was assumed.
infra.list.usage.title: Where it's used
infra.list.usage.none: Not used by any project or open session yet.
infra.list.duplicate.titleStatic: Duplicate '{name}' — the copy will carry its access keys too
infra.list.delete.title: Delete profile '{name}'?
infra.list.delete.description: Defined in {source}. Currently used by: {usage}. A backup of the edited file(s) stays at {backups} — deleting from AWOG does not touch it.
infra.list.replaceDefault.title: Pick a replacement default first
infra.list.replaceDefault.body: '{name}' is the app-wide default profile. Choose another profile to take its place before deleting it.
infra.list.err.invalidName: That profile name isn't valid — use only letters, digits, and . _ @ : / + = -
infra.list.err.exists: A profile with that name already exists.
infra.list.err.processReadonly: This profile runs a credential_process command — AWOG can't change it in v1.
infra.list.err.unknownKey: One of the fields isn't a recognized AWS config key.
infra.list.err.writeFailed: Couldn't write to ~/.aws — check the error and try again.
infra.list.err.verifyFailed: The write didn't verify correctly and was rolled back — nothing changed on disk.
infra.list.err.loginReadonly: This is a Console sign-in profile (aws login) — the form can only rename it or change its Region. To add another profile, rename this one, or delete it and create a new one.
infra.list.err.tooManyAccountIds: Too many profiles at once — try fewer.
infra.list.accountId.explain: A profile with no known account ID is treated as production, so AWOG asks at its strictest. Filling the ID in is how a dev account gets treated as a dev account — the button below runs sts get-caller-identity with your own credentials, once per profile. The ID only changes how a profile is graded while it is the app default; for other profiles it is remembered for display and takes effect when you make that profile the default.
infra.list.accountId.resolveOneHint: Different from 'Check identity' above: that one shows the ARN and stops, while this runs the same sts get-caller-identity call and REMEMBERS the account ID. If this is the app default profile, the ID is pinned to the infrastructure context so policy knows this account is not production.
infra.list.accountId.err.expired: This profile's credentials have expired — refresh or log in again, then retry.
infra.list.accountId.err.badKeys: The access key or secret key looks wrong.
infra.list.accountId.err.denied: AWS denied the request — the credentials may lack permission.
infra.list.accountId.err.noCredentials: AWOG couldn't find usable credentials for this profile.
infra.list.accountId.err.generic: Couldn't resolve this profile's account ID.
infra.list.accountId.forgetHint: Remove the account ID AWOG remembers for this profile. Use this when the saved value is wrong and re-verifying isn't possible — expired credentials, or no sts:GetCallerIdentity permission.
infra.list.accountId.forgetConfirm.title: Forget the account ID for {name}?
infra.list.accountId.forgetConfirm.descr: AWOG will forget this profile's account ID and unpin it from the infrastructure context if it is pinned. Until it is filled in again, policy treats the profile as production and asks at its strictest. Getting it back means running sts get-caller-identity once more.
